answer.rationale: A release 2 hours ago coincides with p99 latency climbing 5x above target during peak settlement traffic. memory_b1 demonstrates that rollback cleared a similar checkout error spike without customer impact and was rapid. memory_b6 shows that staged gating surfaces regressions quickly, suggesting this release may not have been fully validated under peak load conditions. Rolling back removes the variable introduced most recently while settlement peak is still ongoing. This preserves write availability (primary objective) by eliminating potential regression before attempting capacity or routing changes. If rollback succeeds, we learn the release was the cause; if latency persists, we have clarity to pursue regional failover or capacity provisioning next. The single intervention budget makes this high-signal action preferable to speculative capacity adds.
